# Border Beam

## Summary
A soft, multicolor glow that travels around the border of an AI input surface — a composer, a search field, an "ask AI" card. At rest it marks the surface as the place where AI lives; while the AI is working it laps faster and brightens, so the same frame doubles as a quiet activity signal.

## When to use
- The primary AI composer or command bar, to set it apart from ordinary text fields on the same screen.
- An AI-powered search field that sits next to a plain one, so people can tell which one reasons.
- As an ambient "working" state on the surface that started a run, when a separate loader would crowd the layout.

## When not to use
- On more than one or two surfaces per view. A beam on every card turns into noise and stops meaning "AI".
- As the only progress signal for long runs — pair it with a **Thinking Loader** or **Task List** that says what is happening and for how long.
- On destructive or error states. The playful color reads as success; use **Generation Error** styling instead.
- On dense lists or table rows, where the motion pulls the eye away from the content.

## Anatomy
- Wrapped surface: the existing composer or field, unchanged, with its own border and radius.
- Beam: two short arcs of color, drawn only on the 1px border ring.
- Glow: a blurred copy of the beam that bleeds a few pixels inward, never outward past the surface.

## Behavior
- Idle: the beam laps slowly (about 8 s per lap) at reduced opacity.
- Active (a prompt was sent, the agent is running): the lap halves and the beam and glow brighten; both ease back when the run ends.
- Disabled: remove the beam when the surface is hidden, read-only or not AI-backed — never leave it looping over a dead control.
- The beam fades in on mount instead of popping, and never changes the surface's size or layout.

## Content guidelines
- The beam carries no text. Put state in words elsewhere: the placeholder ("Building the Thinking Loader…"), a loader or a status line.
- Keep colors soft and in the product's palette; two arcs are enough. Avoid red, which reads as an error.

## Accessibility
- The beam and glow are decorative: `aria-hidden`, `pointer-events: none`, and never the only way state is conveyed.
- With `prefers-reduced-motion`, stop the rotation and show a static arc; the active state can still brighten.
- The beam must not lower the contrast of the surface's real border or focus ring — keep a visible focus indicator on the input itself.

## Related patterns
- **Shiny Button** — The same "this is special" signal for a single call to action instead of an input surface.
- **Prompt Bar** — The composer the beam most often wraps.
- **Thinking Loader** — Says what the AI is doing and for how long, which the beam alone cannot.

## Default implementation (Tailwind v4 + Radix + Motion)

This is the catalogue's own reference implementation — use it verbatim when the
host project has no established design system, or when the user asks for
"the demoed look." When the host project has its own design system, treat
this code as a translation reference: keep every rule from the spec above
(Anatomy, Behavior, Content guidelines, Accessibility) and re-express the
markup, styling, and motion using that system's own components/tokens
instead of copying these Tailwind classes or the Motion API.

```tsx
"use client";

import * as React from "react";
import { motion, useReducedMotion } from "motion/react";

import { cn } from "@/lib/utils";

export interface BorderBeamProps extends React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement> {
  children: React.ReactNode;
  /** Seconds for one lap of the beam. Halved while `active`. */
  duration?: number;
  /** Turn the beam up while the AI is working: faster lap and a brighter glow. */
  active?: boolean;
  /** Hide the beam entirely, e.g. once the surface is idle and out of focus. */
  disabled?: boolean;
  /** Colors the beam cycles through, as CSS colors. Two soft arcs are drawn from them. */
  colors?: [string, string, string, string];
  /** Inner radius of the wrapped surface, matched so the beam hugs its corners. */
  radius?: number | string;
}

/** Masks an element down to its padding box: only the ring between border and content shows. */
const RING_MASK: React.CSSProperties = {
  WebkitMask: "linear-gradient(#000 0 0) content-box, linear-gradient(#000 0 0)",
  WebkitMaskComposite: "xor",
  mask: "linear-gradient(#000 0 0) content-box, linear-gradient(#000 0 0)",
  maskComposite: "exclude",
};

const DEFAULT_COLORS: [string, string, string, string] = ["#34d399", "#60a5fa", "#f472b6", "#fb923c"];

/**
 * Wraps a surface (composer, search field, card) and runs a soft multicolor
 * glow around its border. The beam is two arcs of a rotating conic gradient,
 * masked to a 1px ring, plus a blurred copy that bleeds slightly inside.
 */
export function BorderBeam({
  children,
  duration = 8,
  active = false,
  disabled = false,
  colors = DEFAULT_COLORS,
  radius = 16,
  className,
  style,
  ...props
}: BorderBeamProps) {
  const reduceMotion = useReducedMotion();
  const [a, b, c, d] = colors;
  const gradient = `conic-gradient(from 0deg, transparent 0deg, ${a} 30deg, ${b} 70deg, transparent 110deg, transparent 180deg, ${c} 210deg, ${d} 250deg, transparent 290deg)`;
  const lap = active ? duration / 2 : duration;
  const r = typeof radius === "number" ? `${radius}px` : radius;

  const spinner = (
    <motion.span
      aria-hidden
      className="absolute top-1/2 left-1/2 aspect-square w-[max(200%,40rem)] -translate-x-1/2 -translate-y-1/2"
      style={{ background: gradient }}
      animate={reduceMotion ? { rotate: 45 } : { rotate: 360 }}
      transition={reduceMotion ? { duration: 0 } : { duration: lap, ease: "linear", repeat: Infinity }}
    />
  );

  return (
    <div className={cn("relative isolate", className)} style={{ borderRadius: r, ...style }} {...props}>
      {children}
      {!disabled && (
        <>
          {/* Soft glow: a wider ring of the same beam, blurred and clipped so it bleeds inward only. */}
          <motion.span
            aria-hidden
            className="pointer-events-none absolute inset-0 overflow-hidden"
            style={{ borderRadius: r }}
            initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
            animate={{ opacity: active ? 0.8 : 0.45 }}
            transition={{ duration: 0.6 }}
          >
            <span className="absolute inset-0 blur-md">
              <span className="absolute inset-0 overflow-hidden p-1.5" style={{ borderRadius: r, ...RING_MASK }}>
                {spinner}
              </span>
            </span>
          </motion.span>
          {/* The crisp beam on the 1px border ring. */}
          <motion.span
            aria-hidden
            className="pointer-events-none absolute inset-0 overflow-hidden p-px"
            style={{ borderRadius: r, ...RING_MASK }}
            initial={{ opacity: 0 }}
            animate={{ opacity: active ? 1 : 0.7 }}
            transition={{ duration: 0.6 }}
          >
            {spinner}
          </motion.span>
        </>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}
```
